title: Therapeutic Potential of Lappula patula Extracts on Germline Development and DNA Damage Responses in C. elegans
content: Lappula patula extracts exhibit significant nematocidal activity, germline disruption, and DNA damage responses in C. elegans. Exposure to increasing concentrations of L. patula extract led to a dose-dependent reduction in worm survival and development, without affecting the high incidence of male phenotype. Further investigation revealed pronounced germline defects, including increased nuclear spacing in the premeiotic tip and pachytene stages, a reduction in DAPI-stained bivalents during diakinesis, and diminished germline size. These defects were accompanied by a significant decrease in brood size, emphasizing the extract’s impact on germline nuclei development. L. patula extracts activated the DNA damage response pathway, as supported by the upregulation of atm-1 and atl-1 expression. Persistent DNA damage triggered apoptosis in a pCHK-1 independent manner in the germline, as indicated by elevated apoptotic cell death during the pachytene stage. Our analysis identified 31 potential anti-tumor compounds within L. patula extracts, characterized by specific fragmentation patterns. The presence of these bioactive components underscores the extract’s cytotoxic properties and highlights its potential as a source of anti-cancer compounds for further investigation. Together, these findings position Lappula patula as a promising candidate for plant-based cancer therapeutics, warranting further exploration.
